note: Source manifest for the ORCH-753 gold cohort. The paper text is NOT committed; it lives at C:/t/eval-fulltext/<PMCID>.txt and gold.load_fulltext refuses a text whose sha256 differs.
citation: Gao J et al. Fungal Melanin Biosynthesis Pathway as Source for Fungal Toxins mBio 2022.
pathway_in_one_line: The DHN melanin pathway in Alternaria alternata, shown by CRISPR deletions to branch at 1,8-DHN into the perylenequinone phytotoxins (altertoxins).
scope_note: In scope: the pentaketide route YWA1/AT4HN -> T4HN -> scytalone -> 1,3,8-THN -> vermelone -> 1,8-DHN, the enzymes PksA, AygA/AygB, Brm1/Brm2, and the paper's own finding that 1,8-DHN is the last common intermediate of DHN melanin and perylenequinone biosynthesis. Adjacent and a real trap: a large amount of the same chemistry is restated for OTHER fungi (Aspergillus fumigatus alb1/ayg1/arp1/arp2/abr1/abr2, Botrytis cinerea BcPks12/13, Bcscd1, Bcbrn1/2). Those sentences name both sides too, so a blind drafter will book them; the gold must record them with the organism they belong to or mark them adjacent. Also adjacent: the alternariol (AOH) pathway and the cmrA transcription-factor regulation, which is interaction rather than chemistry.
selected_because: The best stated chemistry available in a fungus, and the conversions are an ordered chain rather than isolated steps, so a recall failure is diagnosable. It also doubles as a plant-disease-mechanism paper (the products are phytotoxins) without being labelled as one. Second-choice fungal candidate, kept as a fallback: PMC5481523 (sorbicillin biosynthesis in Penicillium chrysogenum, 44,403 chars, ~5 conversions) is cleaner on scope but carries less reaction weight.
